cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Consensus Means Me
cards.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You like the blue campaign poster? I'll tell the volunteers they're happy with me in charge. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The colour, yes. Could we work on the slogan together?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Of course. I'm glad everyone's accepted my collaborative leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's each write one and let the volunteers choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. My first act as campaign leader is to delegate the decision.

mechanism: A calls approval of a poster color a mandate to lead, accepting shared design and volunteer choice as further proof of accepted command.
confusable: Unlike real consensus-building, A treats each limited agreement as settled personal leadership; confidence depends on yielding practical creative control.
comparison: Poster color/slogan vote differ from attendance paired with opposing a budget.
seedUse: Use D71-b blue/slogan/two drafts/volunteers with S02-b adapting control to keep collaborators involved.
